verdict_rationale: No claim exceeds its registered ceiling, no frozen statement was silently edited, no negative was dropped, and every post-landing mutation found is disclosed in-file or in its commit message. The real defects are structural: results artifacts and result-generating code live outside the freeze hash-chain, so the chain cannot see the mutations it exists to record; one committed results file is no longer byte-reproducible from its emitter; and one recorded provenance anchor is unreachable from any ref.

findings.claim_reviewed: the freeze chain governs the capsule's evidence artifacts
findings.evidence_gap: The chain hash-binds the 5 core docs and lane protocol files only. Zero of the 8 exact/results/*.json files are named by any manifest, so post-landing edits to landed results are structurally invisible to verify_freeze_chain. Two such edits exist: D17_RESULTS.json gained an RV-B2(ii) provenance note after first landing (first-landed blob 84b127a7 lacks it; 905a7200 added it together with the T72 oracle repair), and RV_B1_RESULTS.json was edited by 97b38de2 (RV-6/correction). Both edits are disclosed and substantively honest; the defect is that nothing in the chain would have caught an undisclosed one.
findings.fix_hint: At landing time, record each results file's sha256 in the lane freeze (or a small FREEZE_RESULTS manifest amended per result commit), so any later in-place edit becomes recorded drift exactly like a core-doc edit.

findings.claim_reviewed: committed results are the output of their committed checkers
findings.evidence_gap: exact/rv_b1.py line 630 emits where_the_positive_lives = 'query amortisation, measured in multi_query_amortisation above.', but the committed RV_B1_RESULTS.json contains the hand-corrected text plus a correction_C1 block ('raised_by: session lead centre review of the merged artifact'). The committed artifact therefore cannot be regenerated byte-for-byte from its own emitter. Two-host replay (billy-laptop, billy-old; byte-identical outputs on both) shows this is the ONLY non-reproducing results file.
findings.fix_hint: Fold the correction into the emitter (with the original retained as a field, as correction_C1 already does) and regenerate, recording both hashes in the freeze; or mark the file as human-annotated with a schema the emitter itself emits.

findings.claim_reviewed: recorded freeze_commit anchors identify real history
findings.evidence_gap: 11d165b77ada54cc3dbc286f5ecc9369a7560896 (freeze_commit recorded in d19.py, d20.py, D19_RESULTS.json, D20_RESULTS.json) is unreachable from every ref on origin; it survives only as an unreferenced object in long-lived clones. A fresh clone cannot verify what was frozen in that commit. The D19/D20 branch was evidently rebased before merge (merged history diverges from the branch the freeze recorded).
findings.fix_hint: Retarget the four freeze_commit references to the merge commit on main that contains the frozen trees (or record both), via a one-line freeze amendment; going forward, freeze files should record only commits reachable from main.

findings.claim_reviewed: HOSTILE_REGISTRY census is the authoritative hostile list
findings.evidence_gap: H-D19b and H-D20b are declared 'ADDED BY THIS PROTOCOL' inside D19_D20_PROTOCOL_V1.json but were never appended to HOSTILE_REGISTRY_V1.json, whose census in FREEZE_V1 still says hostiles: 27 while ground truth is 29. Fragmented hostile bookkeeping is how a hostile gets silently dropped from a future census.
findings.fix_hint: Append the two rows (with their protocol as origin) and amend the census count.

findings.evidence_gap: All 30 rows read OPEN; 14 carry PROVED_LOCAL certificates in D17_RESULTS since #275. The registry is the natural index for downstream lanes (and D28 hooks) and currently understates landed state.
findings.fix_hint: Additive status amendment: OPEN -> PROVED_LOCAL(D17) for the 14 rows, citing the results file; keep OPEN for the rest.

findings.claim_reviewed: receipts implement the frozen receipt_fields schema
findings.evidence_gap: The frozen schema names 13 field families (B_exec vector, wall/CPU/GPU/IO/storage, provenance supports/alternatives, ambiguity size/entropy, protected round-trip errors, counterexample + version-space shrinkage, reuse identities, active k/N, ...). Landed receipts carry 7 keys; the B_exec vector itself - the programme's core burden object - is absent from every receipt row.
findings.fix_hint: Extend the receipt writers to emit at least B_exec stage counts and wall/CPU per job; or amend the schema to the subset actually promised for D17-D22 and keep the full schema as the D25+ target.

findings.evidence_gap: research/top-tier-atomic-closure-v1/IN_FLIGHT_COORDINATE_MAP_V1.json still marks D21 and D22 as IN_FLIGHT although both landed (PRs #289 and #285 merged at heads 885ccbad / 078dac97); its D23/D24 legality notes and D27 'highest-value unstarted' ranking are being consumed by planning lanes as if current.
findings.fix_hint: One-line status update in that map (D21/D22 -> LANDED with PR refs), or a standing rule that the map is advisory-only with a checked-at date.

findings.evidence_gap: Two coexisting legal patterns: standalone lane freezes (D19/D20, RV-B, and now D23) vs amendments to FREEZE_V1 (D21/D22 protocol). Both verify, but a new lane must now choose per precedent, and census fields in FREEZE_V1 cannot see standalone-lane content.
findings.fix_hint: Document the rule of thumb (standalone freeze for new lane protocols; core amendment only when a frozen core doc itself changes) in the next protocol that freezes.

findings.evidence_gap: oracles_d17.py t72 revocation-target default was switched to true sources by the RV-B2 repair (905a7200), with the legacy 'leaves' mode retained and the D17_RESULTS note added. Fully disclosed, but had emitters been hash-bound (F1) the repair would have required a recorded amendment naming the new oracle hash, making the audit trail automatic rather than commit-message-deep.
findings.fix_hint: Same as F1: bind result-generating code hashes at landing.
